summary_paragraph: A woman with complex bariatric surgical history (prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass with later open reversal) and chronic abdominal pain was admitted for recurrent nausea/vomiting and worsening diarrhea shortly after a recent discharge on oral vancomycin for C. difficile, with concern she was vomiting doses and therefore undertreated. She remained afebrile with no leukocytosis, normal renal function, and a benign abdominal exam; surgery found no acute surgical issue and no new imaging was pursued. She was treated symptomatically with antiemetics and IV fluids, continued on oral vancomycin and acid-suppression/sucralfate regimen, and opioids were avoided inpatient given chronic pain history and concern for impaired motility. Symptoms improved with ability to tolerate oral intake and formed stools by discharge; asymptomatic bacteriuria on urinalysis was not treated. She was discharged home with instructions to complete vancomycin and follow up with GI and pain medicine.
